newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's foreign direct investment soar - reports.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's foreign direct investment soar - reports.

text.p: Foreign direct investment in South Korea totalled $3.69 billion in the first four months of this year, up from $537 million the same period a year ago, local media reported on Sunday.
The Korea Economic Daily newspaper and Yonhap Television News, quoting finance ministry data, said the figure was higher than the $3.20 billion invested during the whole of 1996.
Finance ministry officials were not immediately available for comment.

By sector, the hotel and distribution industry attracted investment of $2.74 billion, up 898.5 percent year-on-year, while the manufacturing sector saw foreign direct investment rise 261.6 percent to $951 million, the reports said.
In April alone, foreign direct investment totalled $1.56 billion -- a monthly record, they said.
The increased foreign investment was attributed to the government's drive to open wider its markets to foreigners.
South Korea, pressured by the widening current account deficit, has been accelerating its market opening policies to attract as much foreign funding as possible.
The country's current account deficit widened to a record $23.72 billion in calendar 1996, from a $8.95 billion shortfall in 1995.
The government has forecast this year's current account deficit at around $18 billion.
